part2.intro: Three students describe the uniform at their school.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Oliver – England
texts.text: At my school we wear black trousers or a black skirt, a white shirt and a dark green jacket with the school name on the pocket. We also have to wear a tie, which I hate because it's so uncomfortable. The worst thing is the price of the jacket – my parents paid sixty pounds for it! But I think a uniform is a good idea, because nobody has to worry about fashion.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Mai – Vietnam
texts.text: At my school, girls wear a white blouse and a dark blue skirt or trousers, and boys wear a white shirt. On Mondays we also wear a red scarf for our school meeting. I like my uniform because it's light and cool when the weather is hot. My mum buys me two new shirts every year because I'm growing quickly. When I finish school, I want to keep my old uniform to remember my friends.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Lucas – Brazil
texts.text: My school doesn't have a strict uniform. We only have to wear a school T-shirt – it's yellow with a blue picture on it – and we can choose our own jeans or shorts. Some students wear really expensive trainers to look cool, which I think is silly. Last year our class had a competition to design a new T-shirt for the school, and mine won! Now everyone wears my design.

items.q: Who wears something extra on one day of the week?
Who says part of their uniform is not comfortable?
Who helped to create their school's uniform?
Who likes their uniform because of the weather?
Who thinks some students care too much about how they look?
Who talks about how much their uniform costs?
Who would like to keep their uniform in the future?

part3.title: Old trainers, new life
part3.text:
When fourteen-year-old Joe Barker's favourite trainers got dirty and broken, his mum told him to throw them away. But Joe didn't want to lose them. Instead, he watched some videos online and learned how to clean and repair them. "They looked almost new when I finished," he says. "I couldn't believe it."

Soon his friends started asking him to clean their trainers too. At first Joe did it for free, but now he asks for between five and fifteen pounds, because some jobs take much longer than others. "Some trainers just need a wash. Others need new laces, or they have holes I have to repair," he explains. He only works in the garage at the weekends, because during the week he has too much homework.

Joe also buys old trainers at second-hand shops, repairs them and sells them online. "Last month I found a pair of white trainers for two pounds. After a few hours of work, I sold them for forty!" He is saving the money for a holiday in Japan, where he wants to visit some famous shoe shops.

His parents are happy about his business, but there is one problem. "We can't park the car in the garage any more," laughs his dad. "There are shoes everywhere!"

Joe thinks more young people should repair their clothes and shoes. "Fashion changes so quickly, and people throw away lots of things. But if you look after your clothes, they can last for years."

items.q: Why did Joe first learn to repair trainers?
options: His mum asked him to do it.
He wanted to keep his favourite pair.
He wanted to start a business.

items.q: How much does Joe ask his friends to pay?
options: the same price for every pair
a different price for different jobs

items.q: When does Joe work on trainers?
What is Joe going to do with the money he makes?
What problem does Joe's dad talk about?
options: Joe spends too much time in the garage.
There is no space for the car.

part4.title: The story of the umbrella
part4.text:
People have {19} umbrellas for more than 3,000 years. The first umbrellas, in China and Egypt, were not for the rain. They kept the sun off important people, like kings and queens.

In Europe, umbrellas only became popular in the 18th century. A British man called Jonas Hanway was one of the first men to carry an umbrella in London. At first people {20} at him, because they thought umbrellas were only for women! But soon many other men {21} his example.

Early umbrellas were very heavy because they were made of wood and thick material. Then, in 1852, Samuel Fox {22} an umbrella with metal parts. It was much lighter and stronger, and we still use the {23} design today.

Now you can buy umbrellas in every colour, and some are small enough to {24} in your pocket or bag. But people still forget them – thousands are left on London buses and trains every year!

items.q: What is the girl going to wear to the concert?

script.t: Dad, what should I wear to the school concert? I was going to wear my long dress.
It'll be really hot in the hall. What about your black skirt?
Hmm, I'd prefer to wear my jeans and my new pink top. The teacher says we don't need to dress smartly.
Fine. That sounds comfortable.

items.q: What did the boy buy for his mum's birthday?

script.t: Did you get a present for Mum's birthday, Tom?
Yes. I wanted to buy her an umbrella because she lost hers, but Dad's already bought her one.
So what did you get?
I looked at some scarves, but they were all too expensive. In the end I got her a purse. Her old one's broken.

items.q: Which boy is Daniel?

options.label: boy in a cap and shorts
boy in a T-shirt and glasses
boy in a coat and glasses

script.t: Which one is your cousin Daniel? Is he the boy in the cap?
No, that's his friend. Daniel wears glasses.
Oh, the one in the long coat?
No, he never wears a coat, even in winter! He's the one in the red T-shirt, next to the door.

items.q: When does the sale finish?

script.t: Do you want to go to the sale at Fashion Corner? I want some new jeans.
Is it still on? I thought it finished last Saturday.
No, the poster in the window says it goes on until Monday.
Great. Then let's go on Sunday – I'm busy tomorrow.

items.q: What must the boy take to school tomorrow?

script.t: Mum, where are my sports shorts? I need them tomorrow.
Isn't PE on Thursday? Tomorrow's Wednesday.
Oh, you're right. But we're going to the park for science, and the teacher says we need trainers, not school shoes.
OK. Take your raincoat too.
I don't need it. It's going to be sunny all day.

part2.intro: You will hear a guide talking to visitors about a fashion exhibition at a museum.
part2.title: Fashion Through Time

items.label: In the last room, visitors can try on:
Designer of the pink suit: Lily

script.t: Welcome to the City Museum. My name's Rachel, and I'm going to tell you about our new exhibition, Fashion Through Time. It isn't on the ground floor with the paintings – you'll find it on the third floor. Take the lift next to the café. The exhibition shows clothes from the last three hundred years. Most people think the oldest thing is the beautiful blue dress near the door, but that's from 1850. Our oldest thing is a pair of brown leather boots from 1720 – they're very small! In the next room there are skirts, tights and shoes from the 1960s. In the last room, you can try on some hats from the past and take photos. Please don't touch the coats and suits, because they're very old. Don't miss the modern room – there's a wonderful pink suit by the young designer Lily Grant. That's G-R-A-N-T. She's only twenty-four! After your visit, you can go to the museum shop. It sells T-shirts, bags and umbrellas with pictures from the exhibition. The museum closes at six o'clock, but the shop closes a little earlier, at half past five.

part3.intro: You will hear Emily talking to her friend Sam about a fashion show at their school.

items.q: What is Emily's skirt made from?
Who made Sam's suit?
Where will the show be if the weather is good?
How much is a ticket for a student?
Who will choose the winner?

script.t: Sam, are you going to be in the fashion show on Friday?
Yes, Mr Ford asked me. I'm a bit nervous. What about you, Emily?
I'm in it too. Everyone has to wear clothes made from old things. I wanted to make a dress from newspapers, but it was too difficult. So my grandma and I made a skirt from old plastic bags!
Cool! I'm wearing a suit made of old maps. My sister made it – she's really good at that kind of thing. Mum wanted to help, but she's too busy at work.
A suit made of maps? I want to see that! Is the show going to be in the school hall?
It was going to be there, but now it's going to be outside in the playground, because more people can come. If it rains, we'll use the sports hall.
And how much are the tickets?
Three pounds for adults and one pound for students. All the money's going to an animal hospital.
Who's choosing the winner? Mr Ford?
No, he's just organising it. Last year it was the head teacher, but this year a woman from a fashion magazine is coming!
Wow! Now I'm really nervous. What shoes are you going to wear?
My black school shoes – they look good with the suit. My trainers are too dirty.
Ha! I'll wear my boots with my skirt.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking about her new glasses.
items.q: How does she feel about her glasses now?
options: worried that people will laugh at her
sorry that she chose that colour

script.t: When the eye doctor said I needed glasses, I was really worried. I thought everyone at school would laugh at me, so I chose some boring brown ones. But on my first day, my friends said they looked great, and now I can see the board clearly. I love them! Next time I might choose a more exciting colour, but these are fine for now.

items.intro: You will hear a boy talking to a shop assistant.
items.q: Why does the boy want to bring back the jacket?

script.t: Hello. I bought this jacket here on Saturday, but I'd like to bring it back.
Is it too small? We've got bigger sizes.
No, the size is fine, and I love the colour. But look – there's a hole in the pocket. I only saw it when I got home.
Oh, I'm sorry. Would you like another one?

items.intro: You will hear a mother talking to her son.
items.q: What does she want him to do?

script.t: Ryan, have you seen your bedroom? There are clothes all over the floor – jeans, socks, your school sweater. And your clean shirts are still on the bed. I've already washed your football shirt, so don't worry about that. But please put everything in your cupboard before dinner. I'm not doing it for you!

items.intro: You will hear two friends talking about a clothes website.
items.q: What does the boy say about the website?
options: It only has clothes for girls.

script.t: Have you tried that new clothes website, Style Teen?
Yes, my sister showed me. There are lots of nice jackets and trainers for boys on it.
And the prices are good, aren't they?
Not really – most things cost more than in the shops. And it's so confusing! I spent twenty minutes trying to find my size and then I gave up.

items.intro: You will hear a teacher talking to her class before a school trip.
items.q: What is the teacher mainly talking about?

script.t: OK, everyone, just a few things about tomorrow's trip to the farm. We'll meet here in the classroom as usual. Now, it's going to be very muddy, so please don't come in your school uniform or your best trainers. Wear old clothes and boots, and bring a raincoat. And put a warm hat in your bag – it can get cold there in the afternoon.

part5.intro: You will hear Oscar talking to his mum after a family holiday. What did each person leave at the hotel?

script.t: Oscar, the hotel phoned. They found lots of our things in the rooms! I can't believe this family.
Oh no! What did they find? Was it Dad's watch? He couldn't find it at the airport.
No, he found his watch in his coat pocket on the plane. But he left his belt on the bathroom door.
Typical! What about Grandma? She's always losing her glasses.
Her glasses are fine – she's wearing them now. It was her umbrella. She left it next to the bed.
And Ruby? I'm sure my sister forgot something.
Yes, her swimming costume. It was still wet, so she put it outside on the balcony and forgot about it.
Uncle Pete said he left his trainers under the bed.
No, he found those when he was packing. But the hotel has got his raincoat. It was in the cupboard by the door.
Well, that's everyone except me. I packed everything really carefully.
Really? Then whose shorts are these? The hotel says they're blue with yellow stars on them.
Oh! They're mine. I wore them on the beach on the last day.
